note: htmx integrates the HTMX JS library with Drupal 11.3+. Version 2.0.x builds on core's full HTMX integration: the Twig function create_htmx() returns a Drupal\htmx\Template\HtmxAttributeBuilder, a Stringable proxy over core's Drupal\Core\Htmx\Htmx class, emitting data-hx-* attributes (get/post/put/patch/delete, target, swap, trigger, select, vals, headers, boost, pushUrl, on, ...). In PHP you use core's Htmx class directly to build both attributes and HX-* response headers (HX-Trigger/HX-Redirect/HX-Location/HX-Push-Url/HX-Reswap/HX-Retarget...) then applyTo() a render array. The module's own HtmxAttribute and HtmxResponseHeaders classes were REMOVED in 2.0.x. Route option _htmx_route:true renders via core SimplePageVariant; /htmx/{entityType}/{entity}/{viewMode} renders an entity fragment (entity.view access); toolbar removed on HX-Request. Site-builder surface: htmx_block config entity (htmx.htmx_block.*, admin /admin/structure/htmx-block, permission administer htmx_block) wrapping a core block plugin, plus the htmx_loader block that lazy-loads it on an event. Views: display plugin id 'htmx' and pager id 'htmx_mini'. Permission: administer htmx_block. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real htmx_block config entities wrapping core block plugins.

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal htmx module (2.0.x), how do I add hx-get / hx-target / hx-swap attributes to an element from a Twig template without writing JavaScript? Name the Twig function and the object it returns.
evals.expected_output: Call the Twig function create_htmx() (from HtmxTwigExtension); it returns an HtmxAttributeBuilder (a proxy over core's Drupal\Core\Htmx\Htmx) that you chain, e.g. create_htmx().get(url).target('#id').swap('outerHTML'), which prints data-hx-* attributes. Attach core/htmx for the JS.

evals.prompt: With the Drupal htmx module 2.0.x, how do I send HTMX response headers (like HX-Trigger or HX-Redirect) from a controller or render array? Which class do I use now?
evals.expected_output: In 2.0.x the module's HtmxResponseHeaders class is gone; use core's Drupal\Core\Htmx\Htmx. Build headers with its methods (addTriggerHeader(), addRedirectHeader(), addLocationHeader(), addPushUrlHeader(), addReswapHeader(), addRetargetHeader(), ...) then call $htmx->applyTo($build), which adds them to $build['#attached']['http_header'].

evals.prompt: The Drupal htmx module can lazy-load a block over HTMX. What config entity / admin page does it add for defining these blocks, which permission guards it, and which block plugin places the loader?
evals.expected_output: It adds an HTMX Block config entity (htmx_block) managed at /admin/structure/htmx-block, guarded by the 'administer htmx_block' permission, plus the 'htmx_loader' (HTMX Loader) block plugin that swaps itself for a chosen HTMX block on a configured event.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has an HTMX Block (htmx module) with machine id 'htmx_med'. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which core block plugin it wraps/loads.
evals.expected_output: htmx.htmx_block.htmx_med wraps the plugin system_powered_by_block (the 'Powered by Drupal' block).

evals.prompt: There is an HTMX Block named 'htmx_med2' configured on this site. Inspect the live htmx_block configuration and state which core block plugin it is set to load.
evals.expected_output: htmx.htmx_block.htmx_med2 wraps the plugin system_branding_block (the Site branding block).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (the htmx module is installed), create an HTMX Block config entity with machine id 'htmx_build' that loads the core 'Powered by Drupal' block (system_powered_by_block). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A htmx.htmx_block.htmx_build config entity exists with plugin: system_powered_by_block. E.g. HtmxBlock::create(['id'=>'htmx_build','plugin'=>'system_powered_by_block','settings'=>[...], 'visibility'=>[]])->save().

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the htmx module to create an HTMX Block with machine id 'htmx_build2' that loads the core Site branding block (system_branding_block). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A htmx.htmx_block.htmx_build2 config entity exists with plugin: system_branding_block.
